question.problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to \pi }[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \frac{4t}{\pi }\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 2+\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \pi }f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(\frac{4t}{\pi })\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi  \\ 1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\ \frac{4\pi }{\pi }\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {lim}_{t\to \pi }g(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(2+\operatorname{tan}⁡t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \pi }\,(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\ (2+\operatorname{tan}⁡\pi ) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi \end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \pi }[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to \pi }f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to \pi }g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =0\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 2+4\cdot (-1) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
